entry.title: Add WebAssembly reference instruction pages
entry.content:
Description

Adds MDN reference pages for the WebAssembly reference instructions: a landing page plus one page per instruction in the spec's "Reference Instructions" section, along with a sidebar entry and a bullet on the WebAssembly reference index.

New pages:

  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference: landing page
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/null: ref.null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/is_null: ref.is_null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/func: ref.func
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/as_non_null: ref.as_non_null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/eq: ref.eq
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/test: ref.test
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/cast: ref.cast

Also updated:

  • files/sidebars/webassemblysidebar.yaml: new "Reference" listSubPages entry under Instructions
  • files/en-us/webassembly/reference/index.md: new "WebAssembly reference instructions" bullet

Motivation

These instructions were missing from MDN's Wasm reference (#37854). As agreed with @chrisdavidmills, the instruction pages follow the structure of the add128 page, and the section follows the Table instructions landing page.

Additional details

How the examples were tested:

  • Each page's interactive example (the WAT and the JS loader exactly as written) was compiled with @mdn/watify, the compiler MDN uses for {%wasm-url%}. It was then run in Node 24 (V8), and the logged output matches the comments in each example.
  • The trapping and edge-case behavior described in the prose was tested with separate modules:
    • ref.as_non_null and ref.cast trap with a RuntimeError (on null, and on a type mismatch).
    • A nullable cast target lets null through.
    • ref.func fails validation without a declaration, and an export or global initializer counts as one.
    • ref.eq treats null as equal to null, compares i31refs by value, and rejects externref operands.
  • The binary encodings come from the WAT compiler's output and match spec §5.4.6. ref.test and ref.cast list both the nullable and non-nullable encodings.
  • lint:md, lint:fm, lint:typos and lint:yml pass. All pages render locally with npm start, with no broken links.

Expected flaw until the BCD data is released: each instruction page reports Unknown browser-compat entry: webassembly.instructions.ref_* for {{Compat}}, and {{Specifications}} is empty, because the keys are added in the BCD PR below.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #37854

We have two documents that have basically identical structure and identical verbiage (presumably the observatory docs copied us, or we both copied from the spec explainer). entry.title: Fix the interactionId collection example
entry.content:
Description

Use a Map consistently in the interactionId example and log the accumulated durations inside the observer callback. Include the interaction ID with each maximum and add context menu and IME composition input to the event table.

Motivation

The example calls .has() on a plain object, which throws when an interaction is delivered. Its logging loop also runs before the asynchronous observer callback collects any entries.

Additional details

Clarify that the example groups observed events, with the default 104 ms duration threshold.

The event table follows the Event Timing interactionId algorithm.

Validation: front-matter lint, Markdown lint and a local Node harness for deferred callbacks, zero IDs, grouping and accumulation across deliveries. Local preview served successfully. Chrome interaction testing was not run.

Related issues and pull requests

No related issue. The pre-submission open PR search for interactionId found no competing change.

entry.content:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the network module:
    • network.setCacheBehavior
    • network.setExtraHeaders
  • Added a "Request modifiers" section to the network module landing page.

Every example was run against Firefox Nightly 159 and Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server, and both browsers behaved the same unless noted below.

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-setCacheBehavior
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-setExtraHeaders

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

  • Compat data for the headers parameter of network.setExtraHeaders:
    • Chrome 155 returns unsupported operation ("Only string headers values are supported") for a "base64" header value (chromium-bidi source), and sends non-ASCII characters in a "string" value as Latin-1 (é as e9) rather than UTF-8 (seen in our test run). Firefox follows the spec on both. BCD shows Chrome's support as complete. cc @OrKoN for the compat sheet update.
    • BCD marks Firefox's support as partial because it "fails to set Unicode headers" (bug 1994996). That bug was fixed in Firefox 150, and Nightly 159 sends UTF-8 correctly. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
  • Spec link for setExtraHeaders. BCD has no spec_url for webdriver.bidi.network.setExtraHeaders and marks it standard_track: false, unlike setCacheBehavior. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update. Until BCD has the URL, the page sets spec-urls in its front matter to fill the Specifications table.

entry.title: Document sticky activation carry-over across same-origin navigations
entry.content:
Summary

Documents the newly specified behavior that sticky activation carries across same-origin navigations: push/replace navigations, reloads, and history traversals (including bfcache restoration) now transfer sticky activation from the predecessor document to the new document, with explicit carve-outs for cross-origin initiators/redirects and for ancestor/descendant frame propagation.

Motivation

The Web platform already specifies and ships this behavior — whatwg/html#11454 is merged and the corresponding Chromium change landed for M142 (intent to ship, commit d8d6786 on the M142 branch; WebKit position positive, mozilla/standards-positions#1295 closed as supportive). Developers relying on the long-standing mental model that "sticky activation dies on navigation" will mis-gate APIs (beforeunload prompts, autoplay, clipboard-change listeners) after multi-page same-origin flows — e.g. a checkout wizard trusting navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive only on the page where the user first interacted.

Changes

  • files/en-us/glossary/sticky_activation/index.md — new paragraph after the activation-triggering events list describing the carry-over semantics, its carve-outs, and linking to the HTML Standard anchor for sticky activation.
  • files/en-us/web/security/defenses/user_activation/index.md — parallel paragraph in the "Comparison between transient and sticky activation" section, stating the same behavior with a spec link and the concrete Chrome 142 ship note.

Both additions are wording-neutral to the rest of each page: existing statements that sticky activation "lasts for the duration of the session" remain true; the new text addresses only the question the glossary page had never covered — what happens to that state when the user navigates.

Verification

  • Read whatwg/html#11454 directly: confirmed merge status, annevk's approval, the shipped-in-Chromium commit, and domenic's authoritative summary of the semantics (same-origin only; no propagation to ancestor/descendant frames; invalidated when a cross-origin document initiates or redirects the navigation; works for push, replace, reload, and both bfcached and non-bfcached traversals except iframes recreated during non-bfcache traversals).
  • Grepped the merged spec source (/tmp/whatwg-html/source, same-origin navigation and user-activation sections) to confirm the behavior's anchor exists (interaction.html#sticky-activation) and does not contradict the doc text.
  • Ensured the specified HTML Standard anchor URL actually exists and resolves.

Related issue

Fixes #41241

Compatibility

Documentation-only change. Behavior described is additive to Chrome 142 and planned in Gecko/WebKit (positive positions; no concrete ship versions yet at time of writing, so the text says "ships in Chrome 142" rather than claiming universal support).

entry.title: Web Storage pages: document storage partitioning (top-level site keying)
entry.content:
Summary

The Web Storage documentation states that localStorage is partitioned "by origin only". Historically accurate, but no longer so: all major browsers now partition third-party storage access so that data written by embedded content is keyed by the top-level site as well as the frame's origin. This PR adds a careful, hedged note explaining that mechanism without making browser-specific or paraphrase-heavy claims the maintainers flagged as risky.

Motivation

Developers relying on origin-keyed-only isolation for localStorage can make incorrect privacy/security assumptions — for example, believing that embedded third-party content shares storage unconditionally with same-origin top-level pages on other sites. Issue #43255 requested this correction.

Changes

  • files/en-us/web/api/window/localstorage/index.md — description and return-value wording changed to not imply origin-only keying.
  • files/en-us/web/api/window/sessionstorage/index.md — the "partitioned by origin only" contrast phrase was removed/rewritten so the two storage areas' difference is described without asserting a now-inaccurate isolation guarantee for localStorage.
  • files/en-us/web/api/web_storage_api/index.md — parallel bullet for localStorage reworded; a new paragraph documents that browsers may additionally key storage by top-level site (state partitioning / storage partitioning), linking to the existing State Partitioning and Storage Access API pages, with explicit hedging so it does not make sweeping browser-specific claims.

Verification

  • Confirmed the affected lines by reading all three source pages at main before editing.
  • Validated wording against the HTML Standard's Web Storage introduction and getter steps (same-site language, storage bottle/holder model) — the spec itself is deliberately agent-cluster agnostic, so the added note is hedged rather than normative.
  • Cited Chrome's storage partitioning and Firefox's State Partitioning docs as implementation background without asserting per-browser behavior MDN cannot verify.

Related issue

Fixes #43255

Compatibility

Documentation-only change; no behavior or code affected.

entry.title: New HTML setters
entry.content:
Description

This documents the static HTML setters as detailed here:
https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/declarative-partial-updates#renewed_html_insertion_and_streaming_methods

I have excluded the streaming APIs (will follow up with that in a future PR), and also excluded TrustedParserOptions (will follow up with that in a future PR).

This is quite a big PR, but most of it is copied and pasted from the existing setHTML() and setHMTLUnsafe() docs with minor updates.

There is a lot of duplication here though so I'm open to ideas of how to structure this better if we want minimal docs in ShadowRoot and CharacterData versions of these docs and leave the main docs to just the Element versions of these APIs and reference it? Or alternatively we could leave most of the docs in setHTML, setHTMLUnsafe and reference those from the other docs?

Motivation

These will be released in Chrome 157 (they are currently available behind a flag) and have also been merged in to the HTML Living standard (whatwg/html#12753)
